newsitem.title: FRANCE: French railways debt plan in slight deficit impact.
newsitem.headline: French railways debt plan in slight deficit impact.

text.p: The government's plan to take a further 20 billion francs off the books of state railway system SNCF will have no effect on public debt levels and only a very slight effect on the public deficit, financial daily Les Echos said on Friday.

Transport Minister Jean-Claude Gayssot said on Thursday the government would lighten the SNCF's debt to 48 billion francs from 68 billion in exchange for a commitment to hire 2,000 new workers over the next two years.

The debt will be transferred into an off-balance sheet debt servicing account of the state. This account has existed since 1990 and already contains about 30 billion of SNCF debt, on which the state pays interest.
The addition of 20 billion francs to the account, serviced at a theoretical level of about five percent, would cost the state an extra 2.5 billion francs a year in interest payments.
The debt servicing account exists in addition to the RFF state holding company, created early this year, which owns the SNCF's infrastructure and 134.2 billion francs of SNCF debt.
The move to transfer the debt would lighten operating costs for the SNCF by about 1.0 to 1.5 billion francs a year, while hiring 2,000 workers would cost about 250 million francs, Gayssot said.
He added that the plan could allow the SNCF to reach break even earlier than 1999 which is its current breakeven target.
SNCF lost 15.2 billion francs in 1996 and expects to lose about two billion this year.
